==English== {{wp}} ===Etymology=== {{dercat|en|ett}} From {{inh|en|enm|market}}, from late {{inh|en|ang|market||market}} and {{der|en|xno|markiet}} ({{der|en|fro|marchié}}); all ultimately from {{der|en|la|mercātus||trade, market}}, from {{m|la|mercor||to trade, deal in, buy}}, itself derived from {{m|la|merx||wares, merchandise}}. {{doublet|en|mart}}. Cognate with {{cog|fy|merk||market}}, {{cog|nl|markt}}, {{cog|de|Markt}}, {{cog|da|-}} and {{cog|no|marked||market}}, {{cog|fo|-}} and {{cog|is|markaður||market}}, {{cog|sv|marknad||market}}. Displaced native {{noncog|ang|stapol}}. ===Pronunciation=== * {{IPA|en|/ˈmɑːkɪt/|a=UK}} ** {{audio|en|En-uk-market.ogg|a=UK}} * {{IPA|en|/ˈmɑɹkɪt/|/ˈmɑɹkət/|a=US}} ** {{audio|en|en-us-market.ogg|a=US}} * {{hyphenation|en|mar|ket}} * {{rhymes|en|ɑː(ɹ)kɪt|ɑː(ɹ)kət|s=2}} ===Noun=== {{en-noun}} # {{senseid|en|gathering of people for trading, often periodic at a set time}} A [[gathering]] of [[people]] for the [[purchase]] and [[sale]] of [[merchandise]], often [[periodic]] at a set [[time]]. #: {{syn|en|mart#Noun|fair}} #: {{ux|en|The right to hold a weekly '''market''' was an invaluable privilege not given to all towns in the Middle Ages.}} #: {{ux|en|There's a '''market''' every Thursday and Saturday in the town square.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1949|author=w:Ludwig Von Mises|title=w:Human Action |passage=The '''market''' is a process, actuated by the interplay of the actions of the various individuals cooperating under the division of labor.}} # {{senseid|en|Q132510}}A relatively spacious outdoor or covered site where [[trader]]s set up [[stall]]s, either temporarily or permanently or semi-permanently, and [[buyer]]s [[browse]] the merchandise. #: {{syn|en|marketplace|bazaar|arcade}} #: {{ux|en|This site on North Street used to be the '''market''', until it was redeveloped.}} #* {{RQ:Allingham China Governess|chapter=Foreword|passage=‘I understand that the district was considered a sort of sanctuary,’ the Chief was saying. ‘{{nb...}} They tell me there was a recognized swag '''market''' down here.’}} # {{senseid|en|grocery store, convenience store, or similar store}} Any physical [[store#Noun|store]] selling [[groceries#Noun|groceries]], such as a [[grocery store]] or [[convenience store]]. #: {{hypo|en|supermarket}} #: {{ux|en|Stop by the '''market''' on your way home and pick up some milk.}} #* {{quote-book |en |year=1999 |last=Mendelson |first=Cheryl |authorlink=Cheryl Mendelson |title=Home Comforts: The Art and Science of Keeping House |publisher=Scribner |page=45-46 |isbn=9780684814650 |passage=Mixes [such as cake mixes, pancake mixes, or sauce mixes] are sometimes a reasonable alternative and sometimes not. {{...}} Pancake mixes often offer no advantages at all. Nonetheless, there are times when you would be foolish not to use a mix. Perhaps a domestic emergency occurs. Perhaps cupcakes must be brought to school tomorrow morning, but when you stop at the '''market''' on your way home from work, you cannot remember whether you have baking powder, cream of tartar, baking soda, nutmeg, cake flour, chocolate, or vanilla on your shelf, or you want to go through the “five items or fewer” line. So you buy the mix. Only a glutton for punishment would do otherwise.}} # {{senseid|en|group of potential or current customers}} A [[group]] of [[potential]] or current [[customer]]s for one's [[product]]. #: {{syn|en|sale}} #: {{ux|en|We believe that the '''market''' for the new widget will be the older homeowner.}} #: {{ux|en|Senior citizens are our core '''market''' at present, and we can't afford to alienate them as we explore other markets.}} #* {{RQ:Mill Political Economy |passage=There is a third thing to be considered: how a '''market''' can be created for produce, or how production can be limited to the capacities of the market.}} # {{senseid|en|region where buyers and demand exist}} A [[geographical]] [[area]] or [[region]] where a certain [[commercial]] [[demand]] exists. #: {{ux|en|Foreign '''markets''' were lost as our currency rose versus their valuta.}} # {{senseid|en|particular system for trading in certain goods}} A formally organized, sometimes monopolistic, system of trading in specified goods or effects. #: {{cot|en|distribution channel}} #: {{ux|en|The stock '''market''' ceased to be monopolized by the paper-shuffling national stock exchanges with the advent of Internet '''markets'''.}} #* {{quote-journal|en|year=1980|journal=InfoWorld|volume=2|issue=20 |passage=As they were approaching bankruptcy from being knocked out of the calculator '''market''', they began development on the first commercially available microcomputer, the Altair.}} #* {{RQ:Economist|date=2014-03-15|volume=410|issue=8878 |title=Turn it off|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20140316165950/http://www.economist.com/news/leaders/21598997-american-regulators-should-block-comcasts-proposed-deal-time-warner-cable-turn-it|passage=If the takeover is approved, Comcast would control 20 of the top 25 cable '''markets''', {{...}}. Antitrust officials will need to consider Comcast’s status as a monopsony (a buyer with disproportionate power), when it comes to negotiations with programmers, whose channels it pays to carry.}} #* {{RQ:Guardian|author=Andrew Roth|title=Trump signs Iran peace plan, claiming deal averts ‘worldwide depression’|date=2026-06-18|url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/jun/17/trump-us-iran-war-mou-deal|author2=Patrick Wintour|passage=Defending the deal, Trump said no US president had ever been as tough on Iran as him, and “there is nothing as smart as the '''market''' – and the '''market''' loves it”.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20261020175418/https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/jun/17/trump-us-iran-war-mou-deal|archivedate=20 October 2026}} # {{senseid|en|sum total traded}} The sum total traded in a process of individuals trading for certain commodities. # {{senseid|en|value or worth}} The price for which a thing is sold in a market; hence, [[value]] or [[worth]]; [[market value]]. #: {{ux|en|Q: What's the '''market''' on such a thing, nowadays?
